research_concepts: primary play types of absent player
methodological_questions: Can the closest pre-absence initiation-profile teammate be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
What sample size and number of absence spells are needed to test redistribution of play-type possessions?
How should regression to the mean and spell selection be handled in usage-redistribution tests?
What derived-label and leakage risks arise when play types are built from play-by-play outcomes?
evidence_establishes: No earlier study records were returned by retrieve_history (n_results = 0). The retrieval therefore establishes nothing about prior findings on this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether closest-profile teammates absorb the absent player's play types in any prior analysis by this project.
Whether the stated criteria (initiation profile, minutes, or same-position minutes) are a valid or consistent definition of 'closest'.
Any effect size, direction, or power estimate for this question.
own_inferences: The data hold 148 spells but only 11 independent absence cases. Spells from the same absence are not independent, so the effective sample is about 11, which is too small for a reliable test of a teammate-level 'largest gainer' claim.
The question names three alternative definitions of 'closest' (initiation profile, minutes, same-position minutes). Testing whichever gives the best result would be a forking-paths problem.

Play types and initiator labels are derived from play-by-play outcomes, including points. Using the same outcomes to define the play types and to measure gains creates outcome-derived label and leakage risk.
Absences are not randomly assigned. Injuries and rotation changes are likely to coincide with other lineup changes, so attributing redistribution to the absence alone is confounded.
Player usage is volatile, so the largest post-absence gain may often be a regression-to-the-mean artifact of a teammate's usual variability rather than a substitution effect.
uncertainties: The exact operational definitions of 'initiation profile', 'primary types', and 'largest gainer' are not given in the task.

Season-level coverage of the 2025-26 regular season and playoffs at the 2026-11-01 cutoff: the regular season is complete from 2026-04-13 and the playoffs from 2026-06-21, so both should be complete by the cutoff, but the data must be verified.
The number of absences per team and whether the 11 cases are distinct players or repeated players is not stated.
Whether the play-by-play-derived play-type labels have been validated against manual or tracking data is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: No historical records were returned, so the decision rests on the task statement and the data description alone. The small number of independent absence cases (11) and the ambiguous definition of 'closest' are the main reasons for not proceeding as posed.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 independent absence cases are available, against 148 spells. A test of whether the closest teammate is the largest gainer would have very low power and could not give reliable inference.
Primary play-type exposure for the absent player and for candidate teammates is sparse per spell, so per-type gains are noisy.
Play types are derived from play-by-play outcomes, including points, so the labels and the gain measures are not independent.
Three alternative definitions of 'closest' and several play types create many possible comparisons with no pre-specified primary test.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. No prior work is relied on.

risks.text: 11 independent absence cases give very low power for a claim about the single largest gainer.
Per-spell play-type possessions for the absent player and teammates may be too few for stable gain estimates.
Play-type labels and initiation-profile similarity may have low test-retest reliability across seasons and spells.
Absence spells may be selected on injury or on a unusual usage spike, so post-absence gains can partly reflect regression to the mean.
Play types built from play-by-play outcomes, including points, can make gains partly a function of the outcomes being measured.
If the closest-profile teammate is defined using data from after the absence, the definition leaks the outcome. The profile must use only pre-absence data.
Lineup changes, coaching changes, and opponent quality that coincide with absences can produce gains unrelated to the absence.
Three alternative 'closest' definitions and several play types create forking paths.
Some teammate will always gain the most in any absence, so 'largest gainer' has a high baseline rate that a naive test may mistake for support.
Play-type or initiator attribution errors in play-by-play data would misassign possessions.
Usage and role patterns change across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooling seasons may mix different regimes.
No placebo comparison (for example, non-absence stretches) is specified, so the result cannot be checked against a null.

design.estimand: Not proceeding as posed. The minimum viable test is a descriptive estimate of the share of the absent player's play-type possessions absorbed by each teammate, with an uncertainty interval, and the rank of the pre-specified closest-profile teammate in that distribution.
design.unit: Absence spell (team-season-absent player), with spells grouped by absence event for inference.
design.sample: All 11 absence cases, with spells clustered within absence event; no pooling across alternative 'closest' definitions.
design.power: Not computed. With 11 clusters the design can only detect very large effects, and a null result would be uninformative.
design.controls: Pre-absence usage baseline for each teammate, minutes-matched comparison, and a non-absence placebo stretch for each player. Profile defined only from pre-absence data.
design.falsification: A placebo test using non-absence stretches in which the same 'largest gainer' ranking should not hold above chance.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one definition of 'closest' (initiation profile) and one primary play-type set; treat minutes and same-position minutes as secondary.
design.decision_rule: Report the rank and interval of the pre-specified closest teammate against the placebo distribution. Make no causal or 'largest gainer' claim unless the interval excludes the placebo distribution and the result is robust to the definition choice.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs, as available at 2026-11-01. The 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13 and the playoffs from 2026-06-21. Verify completeness and freeze the play-type derivation version before analysis.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
